correctness.rationale: The published Klazar–Luca recurrence comparisons and product-poset antichain bound extend to base 3; verified the missing parameter window by choosing α=7/20 with α>1/3 and 3^α<3/2 (equivalent 2^20<3^13). Exact binomial Chernoff/entropy upper tail shows strings with ≥αn zero digits are ≤3^n e^(−cn). With fewer zeros, at least r≈(1−α)n nonzeros and known recurrence estimates force n·2^{m−n}≈3^n and only O(1) possible recurrence indices m per n. For a common r-digit prefix and fixed m, comparable distinct suffixes in {0,1,2}^{n−r} produce nonzero Keith-sequence difference M both ≳(3/2)^n and <3^{αn+1}, impossible. Hence suffixes form antichain of size O(3^{n−r}/√n); counting prefixes gives O(3^n/√n) n-digit Keith numbers and K_3(x)≪x/√log x. Finite examples are not infinite proof.
